h: Great Joy Grows From Awe and an Upright Heart

p: in the morning, "on which the soul rejoices";
"the joy of the harvesters of the field";
and at night we say, "chedvah sagi,"
meaning great joy, or much joy.
To understand what the expression "chedvah sagi" means:
הָעִנְיָן הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁמָּצִינוּ בַּפָּסוּק
the matter follows what we find in the pasuk
for the joy of Hashem is your strength."
וַיֵּלְכוּ כָל הָעָם לֶאֱכוֹל וְלִשְׁתּוֹת וְגוֹ׳
"And all the people went to eat and drink" etc.
כִּי הֵבִינוּ בַּדְּבָרִים וְגוֹ׳ (שָׁם ח, יב)
for they had understood the words" etc. (Nechemiah 8:12).
That is, the completeness of joy in holiness
is when it comes out of yirah,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר (תַּנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פֶּרֶק ג)
in the manner of what he said (Tanna d'Vei Eliyahu Rabbah 3):
And this is as written, "They shall rejoice in Your Kingship":
וְאִם אֲדוֹנִים אָנִי אַיֵּה מוֹרָאִי (מַלְאָכִי א, ו)
"And if I am a master, where is My fear?" (Malachi 1:6).
And when one pictures to himself
שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
that the King of the kings of kings, HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
stands over him and sees his deeds,
the fear will immediately come to him, etc.
(Hagahah at the beginning of Orach Chaim).
to straighten the crookedness of the heart,
'And God has made it so that they fear Him.'"
And once one merits, through yirah,
as is written (end of the first chapter of Taanis, 15a):
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וּלְיִשְׁרֵי לֵב שִׂמְחָה (תְּהִלִּים צז, יא)
as it says, 'And for the upright of heart, joy'" (Tehillim 97:11).
And this is the completeness of joy.
And this is what it says (Nechemiah 8:9),
"For all the people were weeping" etc.
teshuvah and remorse came to them,
שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
that the King of the kings of kings, HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
stands over him and sees his deeds,
against His will, blessed be His Name.
"The goal of wisdom is teshuvah," etc.,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר רֵאשִׁית חָכְמָה יִרְאַת ה׳ וְגוֹ׳
as it says, "The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem" etc.
And likewise it is expounded (Avodah Zarah 19a)
עַל פָּסוּק אַשְׁרֵי אִישׁ יָרֵא אֶת ה׳
on the pasuk "Fortunate is the man who fears Hashem"
fortunate is he who does teshuvah
while he is still a man in his vigor.
דִּתְשׁוּבָה בָּא עַל יְדֵי יִרְאָה כָּאָמוּר
For teshuvah comes through yirah, as stated.
And this is what he said to them,
וְאַל תֵּעָצֵבוּ כִּי חֶדְוַת ה׳ הִיא מָעוּזְּכֶם
"And do not be sad, for the joy of Hashem is your strength":
שֶׁמְּבִיאָה לִידֵי יְשָׁרוּת לֵב וְשִׂמְחָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
which brings to uprightness of heart and joy, as mentioned above,
זֶה הוּא גַּם שִׂמְחַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
this is also the joy of Hashem Yisbarach;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג צב, א)
And as written in the holy Zohar (III 92a):
He sends you strength and might,
And this is what is written afterward,
for they had understood the words" etc.:
the joy that comes through yirah
And likewise the three Shabbos meals,
which the holy Arizal, of blessed memory, arranged
to correspond to the holiness of the three Avos:
and the meal of the night of Shabbos Kodesh
corresponds to Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
and it is the meal of the Field of holy Apples,
the spreading of the canopy of peace.
this is the revelation of the Shechinah.
And the joy that comes out of this yirah
and therefore we say at this meal,
"What is 'to one who has nothing prepared'?
to one who did not make an eruv tavshilin."
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאָז חָל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בַּשִּׁשִּׁי
That is, Rosh HaShanah then fell on Friday,
and he said to them, "Go, eat rich foods,"
regarding the second day of Rosh HaShanah,
"and send portions to one who has nothing prepared"
to one who did not make an eruv tavshilin.
And this is what is written there,
"And all the people went to eat and drink
the joy at the meal of Shabbos night
and this is "Great joy will come."

paragraphs.text: Source of the quoted words: Beitzah 15b — “מאי ״לאין נכון לו״? אמר רב חסדא: למי שלא הניח עירובי תבשילין. איכא דאמרי: מי שלא היה לו להניח עירובי תבשילין, אבל מי שהיה לו להניח עירובי תבשילין ולא הניח …” — “§ Since the baraita mentions the verse from Nehemiah, the Gemara poses the following question: What is the meaning of: “Send portions to him for whom nothing is prepared” (Nehemiah 8:10)? Rav Ḥisda said: Send to one who does not …”
